subject: Region fidelity and subprocessor census for DPA acceptance
messages:
From: Emma Blake <emma@cobaltinsurance.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james@cloudops.cobalt.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region fidelity and subprocessor census for DPA acceptance

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the initial conversations last week. Cobalt is preparing to finalize the DPA addendum and we need a short operations acceptance pack before Legal will sign. Specifically we need:

- Confirmation of region fidelity: for our EU and APAC customers we require that data-at-rest and inference processing are pinned to the requested region for normal processing, and an explanation of temporary failover windows, with maximum duration and triggers.
- Subprocessor census: a simple roster (name, role, region, data access scope) of all third parties that will process customer inference requests and operational telemetry.
- Evidence summary: SOC 2 or equivalent controls that cover logging/retention, KMS usage, and access review cadence.

Can you provide an ops checklist we can pass to procurement and legal? Timeline goal is to have sign-off within two weeks (by Oct 5).

Attachment: none yet — we can take files via Drive/DocuSign.

Thanks,
Emma Blake
Director, Cloud Security
Cobalt Insurance
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@cobaltinsurance.com>
Cc: James Park <james@cloudops.cobalt.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region fidelity and subprocessor census for DPA acceptance

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. I've put together a lightweight ops acceptance checklist (summary below) and attached a runbook we use internally. High level answers:

1) Region fidelity: Redwood supports region pinning for hosted workloads. Normal processing is kept in the pinned region. Temporary failover for availability or catastrophic maintenance can occur; typical failover window is up to 72 hours, with shorter windows for edge cache-only hops (12–48h). We always notify customers and include the failover window in the DPA addendum.

2) Subprocessor census: see attached CSV (subprocessor_roster.csv). The file includes name, service type, region, and access scope.

3) Evidence: summary SOC 2 controls, KMS usage notes, and log retention policy are referenced in the attached runbook. For legal we can provide SOC reports under NDA or a signed evidence transfer.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll upload the runbook and roster to the Drive link (below).
- Marissa, can you prepare the DPA addendum draft with the 72-hour failover clause and the subprocessor appendix?
- Emma/James: confirm whether 72h is acceptable or if you require a shorter SLA for targeted subcomponents (e.g., analytics telemetry).

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-residency-evidence
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/8942

I’ll attach the runbook and roster in a follow-up email.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Region fidelity and subprocessor census for DPA acceptance

Emma — looping in Legal ops.

Karthik: looks good. For the DPA addendum I'll draft language that:
- Defines "region fidelity" for inference processing and telemetry (normal vs. exceptional processing).
- Adds a subprocessor appendix that mirrors the roster you provided and allows for 30-day notice for subprocessor changes (or immediate notice for security-critical swaps).
- Explicitly states that transient cache hops (edge pop) are excluded from the pin if no persistent storage outside region occurs, with a maximum transient duration of 48h.

Emma/James — I'll share a redline by EOD tomorrow (Sep 22). To expedite signing we can accept a DocuSign signature page for the addendum, and attach the roster as an annex.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Blake <emma@cobaltinsurance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Cobalt Legal <cobalt-legal@cobaltinsurance.com>, James Park <james@cloudops.cobalt.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region fidelity and subprocessor census for DPA acceptance

Marissa/Karthik — thanks. A few clarifying asks from Legal and CloudOps:

- Is KMS keying per-customer and can we require customer-managed keys for EU accounts? If not, provide exact KMS region and whether keys ever leave the region for backup or key-rotation operations.
- Audit/logging: retention window we need is 365 days for request-level logs; confirm current retention and whether archive exports can be delivered on request.
- Subprocessor visibility: we need the roster in CSV + an attestation email from the named subprocessor owners confirming they will not copy customer inference payloads to other jurisdictions.

On timing: DocuSign sign-off on the addendum is fine; we'd like the roster and attestation in hand before we countersign.

On quoting previous note:
> On Mon, Sep 21, 2026 at 11:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> > 1) Region fidelity: Redwood supports region pinning for hosted workloads. Normal processing is kept in the pinned region. Temporary failover for availability or catastrophic maintenance can occur; typical failover window is up to 72 hours...

We can accept 72h for core inference only if KMS is resident and customer-managed keys are available for EU accounts. Otherwise we need 24h for core inference and 72h for edge-only cache hops.

Best,
Emma
Director, Cloud Security
Cobalt Insurance
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@cobaltinsurance.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james@cloudops.cobalt.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region fidelity and subprocessor census for DPA acceptance

Emma — quick technical reply and attachments.

1) KMS: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for EU and US enterprise accounts. Keys are stored in the customer-selected cloud region and our backups do not export key material outside that region; key-rotation metadata may be processed outside the region but never key material.

2) Logs: default request-level retention is 180 days; we can enable 365-day retention for account-level cohorts and provide export on request. Exports are delivered over a secure SFTP/Drive transfer and we keep a signed export manifest.

3) Subprocessor attestations: attached is subprocessor_roster.csv and a short attestation template we request subprocessors to sign. Where subprocessors operate globally we include region-bound service descriptors in the CSV.

Attachments (stubs):
- residency_runbook_v1.pdf (operational runbook: region pinning, failover playbook, notification cadence)
- subprocessor_roster.csv (name, role, region, access scope, attestation status)
- signed_dpa_summary.pdf (redline summary and proposed DocuSign page)

If Emma confirms CMK is acceptable we can move to a 72h failover window for core inference; otherwise we'll mark core inference 24h in the addendum.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if you'd like to walk through the runbook.

— Soojin Lee
Principal Engineer, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
